p: twelfth year: Which was the first year of the general captivity under Zedekiah.
lion of the nations: Thus the scriptures compare tyrants to cruel and huge beasts which devour all that are weaker than they and such as they may overcome.
trouble the waters with thy feet: You prepared great armies.
with thy height: With heaps of the carcass of your army.
swimmest: As the Nile overflows in Egypt, so will I make the blood of your host overflow it.
put thee out: The word signifies to be put out as a candle is put out.
darkness upon thy land: By this manner of speech is meant the great sorrow that will be for the slaughter of the king and his people.
pomp of Egypt: This came to pass in less than four years after this prophecy.
their waters deep: That is, of the Chaldeans your enemies, who will quietly enjoy all your conveniences.
cast them down: That is, prophecy that they will be cast down: thus the Lord gives his prophets power both to plant and to destroy by his word, read Jer 1:10.
in beauty: Have not other kingdoms more beautiful than you perished?
she is delivered to the sword: That is, Egypt.
him out of the midst of: To make the matter more sensible, he brings in Pharaoh whom the dead will meet and marvel at him, read Isa 14:9.
Elam and all her multitude around: Meaning the Persians.
living: Whom in his life all the world feared.
Meshech: That is, the Capadocians and Italians or Spaniards, as Josephus writes.
of the uncircumcised: Who died not by cruel death but by the course of nature, and are honourably buried with their coat of armour and signs of honour.
north: The kings of Babylon.
comforted over all his multitude: As the wicked rejoice when they see others partakers of their miseries.
terror in the land of the: I will make the Egyptians afraid of me, as they caused others to fear them.
